## 1. Entry points and launch surface

| Path | What it is | State |
|---|---|---|
| `portal/app.py` | The Flask application. `create_app()` builds it; the `__main__` block calls `_ensure_storage_dirs()`, `create_app()`, `development_host(Config.HOST)`, `_print_storage_map()`, then `app.run(...)`. | The real entry point. |
| `run_portal.bat` | One-line batch wrapper: `python portal\app.py`. | Exists, works, but names the program **"L2-COS Operations Portal v1"** — the program is Dispatch. Provides no Stop, Restart, status, or PID handling. |
| `run_sync.bat` / `run_sync.py` | VPS sync helper (`sync/`). | Unrelated to portal lifecycle. |
| `run_bootstrap_d_drive.bat` / `bootstrap_d_drive.py` | One-time migration of project material to the `D:\` tree. | Unrelated to portal lifecycle. |
| `setup_dispatch_folders.ps1` | Creates the `D:\Dispatch Operations`, `D:\Archive`, `D:\Memory` tree and sets five environment variables via `setx`. Idempotent, has `-DryRun`. | Good prior art for the Windows-native style this repository already uses. |
| `cin_lite/run.py` | The govcon pipeline CLI (`dispatch` console script). | Separate subsystem. |
| `portal/cli.py` | `cin-portal-init-admin` — one-time Authority PIN bootstrap. | Required before anything past `/login` is reachable. |

**Finding:** there is no Stop, no Restart, no status display, no PID tracking, and no
launch-failure reporting anywhere in the repository. Task 1 is building the first one.

## 2. Configuration loading

`portal/config.py` is the single configuration surface.

- `Config.HOST` ← `PORTAL_HOST`, default `127.0.0.1`; `Config.PORT` ← `PORTAL_PORT`, default `8080`.
- `Config.SECRET_KEY` ← `PORTAL_SECRET_KEY`, default `dev-portal-key-change-in-production`.
- Session cookie policy is set: `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True`, `SAMESITE="Lax"`,
  `SECURE` gated on `PORTAL_COOKIE_SECURE=1`, `PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME` from `PORTAL_SESSION_HOURS`.
- `is_development_mode()` reads `DISPATCH_MODE` and **defaults to operational**.
- `check_secrets()` raises `InsecureConfigurationError` in operational mode when
  `PORTAL_SECRET_KEY` or `DISPATCH_EMAIL_SECRET` is unset or still the published default.
  It is called from `create_app()`, so nothing reaches a route without passing it.
- `development_host()` pins a development-mode process to the loopback interface.

**Consequence for Task 1:** the launcher must be able to tell Mike *which named setting*
is blocking a start, and must never print the value. It must also read host and port
through the same resolution path rather than assuming `127.0.0.1:8080`.

## 3. Secret handling

Two signing secrets exist: `PORTAL_SECRET_KEY` (Flask session) and `DISPATCH_EMAIL_SECRET`
(HMAC for decision, stakeholder, and IFTA links). Both have published defaults in this
repository, and `_PUBLISHED_DEFAULTS` in `portal/config.py` is the list. `dispatch/tokens.py`
adds an operational-token ledger with its own expiry and revocation.

No secret is written to disk by the application. **Everything new in this mission must
keep that true** — launcher logs, connector audit records, and proof reports all redact
by setting name.

## 4. Path resolution — the five roots

| Root | Resolution order |
|---|---|
| Portal data | `PORTAL_DATA_DIR` → `DISPATCH_OPERATIONS_ROOT/Current Workspace/PortalData` → `portal/data` (`portal/models/__init__.py::get_data_dir`) |
| Database | Same order, then `/dispatch.db` (`dispatch/db.py::_default_db_path`), overridable in-process by `set_db_path()` |
| Evidence uploads | `PORTAL_UPLOAD_DIR` → `DISPATCH_MEMORY_ROOT/Evidence` → `<data dir>/uploads` (`portal/config.py::_resolve_upload_dir`, `dispatch/services.py::_get_upload_dir`) |
| Memory | `DISPATCH_MEMORY_ROOT` → data dir (`get_memory_dir`) |
| Archive | `DISPATCH_ARCHIVE_ROOT` → data dir (`get_archive_dir`); the CIN contract archive is `cin_lite/archive.py::ARCHIVE_ROOT` |

`portal/app.py::_ensure_storage_dirs()` creates the sub-tree under each root at startup
**only when the corresponding environment variable is set**. With no variables set, the
application silently uses `portal/data` inside the repository. That is the single most
important fact for Task 1's display requirement: showing a configured root is not the same
as showing the root Dispatch actually used, and §3.3 asks for the latter.

## 5. Database and lifecycle

Single SQLite file, `sqlite3` from the standard library, no ORM. `get_connection()` opens
WAL, enforces foreign keys, and runs `_init_db()` — `_SCHEMA` (25 Current Reality tables),
then guarded idempotent `ALTER TABLE` migrations, then `init_spine_schema(conn)` and
`init_token_schema(conn)`.

`dispatch/spine/` is the authoritative lifecycle engine (CF-04, adjudicated 2026-08-23):
25 states, `state.transition()` is the only function that may compute a transition and
`store.apply_transition()` the only one that may persist one. `dispatch/opportunities.py`
is advisory and correlates to a Spine work item rather than holding its own stage.
`loads.status` remains the live operational load-status system and is not replaced.

## 6. Backup and restore

`dispatch/backup.py` (with `scripts/dispatch_backup.py` as its CLI, `BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY.md`
as its procedure) already provides `create_backup`, `verify`, `restore`, `capture_environment`,
and `sha256_file`. It uses `sqlite3.Connection.backup()` rather than a file copy, refuses a
non-empty destination, rehomes absolute evidence paths on restore, and records secrets by
name only as `<redacted, not exported>`.

**Consequence:** Task 2 steps 19–20 reuse this rather than building a second backup path,
and Task 1's backup-status display reads its manifest. Per §3.3 the launcher must not call
a backup valid unless a restore verification record exists.

## 7. Windows environment facts — what the repository can and cannot tell us

**Establishable from the repository:**

- Python `>=3.11` (`pyproject.toml`); CI runs 3.11, 3.12, 3.13.
- Runtime dependencies: `flask>=3.0`, `paramiko>=3.0`. Optional: `anthropic>=0.40` (agents), `pytest>=8.0` (dev).
- Service model: a foreground development server (`app.run`). There is no WSGI server,
  no Windows service wrapper, and no process supervisor anywhere in the repository.
- The intended storage layout is the `D:\` tree created by `setup_dispatch_folders.ps1`,
  driven by five environment variables persisted with `setx`.
- Console scripts installed by `pip install -e .`: `dispatch`, `cin-portal`, `cin-sync`,
  `cin-portal-init-admin`.

**Not establishable — carried to the completion report as Mike-only questions (§8 item 11):**

1. Which Python interpreter is on `PATH`, and whether `python` or `py -3.11` is the working invocation.
2. Whether Dispatch is installed with `pip install -e .` or run from the repository directory.
3. Whether the five `DISPATCH_*` / `PORTAL_*` environment variables are actually set on the machine.
4. Whether port 8080 is free.
5. Whether `D:` exists and is writable, and whether the folder tree has been created.
6. Whether real values for `PORTAL_SECRET_KEY` and `DISPATCH_EMAIL_SECRET` are set (without them, operational mode refuses to start).
7. Whether the Authority PIN identity has been bootstrapped.

## 8. Task 3 path reachability — **the mission's §2 item 5 check, answered**

**Result: `ABSENT`. The Sandbox was not read, and could not be.**

This session executes in an isolated Linux container. `D:\Sandbox\Play Pen` and
`D:\Sandbox\Play Pen\Dispatch` are Windows paths on Mike's machine. Checked and found
absent: `/d`, `/mnt/d`, and every entry under `/mnt` (`attach`, `skills`, `user-data` —
none is a Windows volume). `uname -a` reports `Linux vm 6.18.44-fc-v21 … x86_64`.

There is no mount, no network path, and no credential in this environment that reaches a
user's local Windows machine. This is an environment boundary, not a permission that
could be granted, and it was independently corroborated during the earlier
cross-repository audit.

**Therefore the output folder was not created, nothing was read, and no claim about the
Sandbox's contents appears anywhere in this mission's output.** What Task 3 delivers
instead is exactly what §5.2 anticipates — the read-only inventory and classification
tooling, in the repository, with tests proving it performs no write against its input
path — plus the exact command Mike runs on his own machine and the nine outputs in
template form so their shape is inspectable before he runs them.

## 9. Existing external-integration surface

| Area | What exists | Honest status today |
|---|---|---|
| Email / SMTP | `cin_lite/email_delivery.py` — the program's sole mail transport. Real SMTP when `DISPATCH_SMTP_*` is set; otherwise writes `.eml` files to an Outbox. | `UNCONFIGURED` by default |
| Outlook | Referenced only in `dispatch/opportunities.py` (scheduling-fit evaluation). No client, no API call, no credential path. | `UNCONFIGURED` |
| SAM.gov | `cin_lite/acquisition.py`, `DISPATCH_SAM_API_KEY`. | `UNCONFIGURED` by default |
| Claude API | `cin_lite/agents/`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; deterministic fallbacks when absent. | `UNCONFIGURED` by default |
| Accounting | `dispatch/accounting_export.py` — file export, no provider. | `UNCONFIGURED` |
| Route Risk | `route_risk/engine.py` — evaluation logic; `route_risk_events` table. **No feed of any kind.** | `UNCONFIGURED` |
| ELD / HOS / GPS / traffic / weather / load boards / mapping | **Nothing.** No client, no credential, no schema. | `ABSENT` |

Task 4 gives all of these one governed boundary and makes each report its status truthfully
instead of each caller inventing its own answer.

## 10. Jules portal review (§2 item 4)

Inspected for presentation and cockpit ideas relevant to the launcher status display only.
The idea worth carrying is the single-glance status panel: one screen, labelled rows, no
navigation required to see whether the system is up.

**Adopted: nothing else.** Not its runtime, not its security model, not its state handling,
not its static sample behavior, not its simulated upload behavior. The Jules portal is a
read-only design archive; `Dispatch/portal/` is Dispatch.

## 11. Test layout and the bar this mission must clear

`pytest.ini` sets `testpaths = tests`, `python_files = test_*.py`, `addopts = -q`.
`tests/conftest.py` supplies four autouse fixtures: `_scrub_env` (clears every integration
variable, then sets **real** test values for the two signing secrets so the suite exercises
`check_secrets()` rather than bypassing it), `tmp_archive` (redirects archive, outbox,
pending, and portal-data writes into `tmp_path`), and `_csrf_aware_test_client` (installs a
`FlaskClient` subclass that carries the CSRF token, so HTTP tests run with the protection on
rather than around it).

**The bar, restated:** 0 failed / 0 skipped / 0 warnings, coverage not below 93.73%.
No test may be skipped, weakened, or removed to accommodate anything in this mission.
